pager.go:*pager.initNewDB.note: in-memory databases only; a database in a file is created by createIfEmpty

pager.go:*pager.leafLimits.note: one leaf rule per file instead of one per page

pager.go:*pager.leafLimitsFor.note: the file's leaf rule for a given usable size

pager.go:*pager.lockDBForCreate.note: flock upgrade with drop-and-retry between several creators, on the open's busy-handler count; also the exclusive lock of a hot-journal playback

pager.go:*pager.lockDBShared.note: shared DB-file flock, repeated through the busy handler; ErrBusy when it gives up

pager.go:*pager.newPage1.note: header and empty leaf image of page 1

pager.go:*pager.notePage1Read.note: dbFileVers from a page-1 read, 0xffffffff after a failed one

pager.go:*pager.open.note: page 1 and the page count are read at one snapshot in readPage1AtOpen

pager.go:*pager.page1FrameHeader.note: the plaintext header of page 1's WAL frame, for the format checks that come before the key's (drift-2026-11-24-3)

pager.go:*pager.page1Hook.note: under a key, page 1's failed authentication at open is kept from the integrity hook until it is known to be damage (drift-2026-11-24-3)

pager.go:*pager.page1OnChange.note: schema format 6 and later write page 1 only when needed

pager.go:*pager.page1Unauthenticated.note: a page 1 that fails its authentication at open, judged after the header and the page count: ErrWrongKey unless another page proves the key or could not be read; SQLCipher returns SQLITE_NOTADB for both (sqlcipher.c:3263-3295, btree.c:3306, 3361-3362, v4.14.0; drift-2026-11-24-3)

pager.go:*pager.pagerError.note: a failed commit's end: the state and the cleanup at once. errCode is the commit's error, or, when its fetch of page 1 met a failed spill, the one pagerStress set already; pagerError trips the cursors with it and clears it (drift-2026-11-24-5). SQLite's failed WAL commit never enters PAGER_ERROR: pagerWalFrames returns the error (pager.c:6512, 3219-3236), pager_error stores only IOERR/FULL (pager.c:1955-1958), and the transaction is rolled back as any other (sqlite3PagerRollback, pager.c:6779-6782), its cursors tripped with SQLITE_ABORT_ROLLBACK (btree.c:4524-4533). A failed spill only records the error (pagerStress, pager.errCode) and rollbackLocked cleans up

pager.go:*pager.pagerStress.note: a failed write stores pager.errCode and sets pagerError, pager_error's part (pager.c:1947-1960), inline

pager.go:*pager.proveKeyAtOpen.note: tries up to keyProbePages other pages of the database (up to lockBtreePageCount's size) under the open's key, and keeps the first read error; no SQLCipher counterpart (drift-2026-11-24-3)

pager.go:*pager.readHeaderCounters.note: page-1 counters at the newest committed state, for Open; a transaction has its snapshot's (readHeaderCountersAt, the counters memo)

pager.go:*pager.readPage1AtOpen.note: open-time page-1 read and page count under one WAL read transaction

pager.go:*pager.readRawPage1Header.note: page 1's header alone, for a page 1 the codec sweep cannot read whole

pager.go:*pager.refreshHeaderFromPage1.note: page-1 re-read at write begin after a peer's change: one source, whole page, lockBtree's page-count rule

pager.go:*pager.returnLent.note: any-store: the last cursor off a lent slab buffer returns it (drift-2026-11-21-25)

pager.go:*pager.rollbackLocked.note: in pagerError it first trips the cursors with pager.errCode (sqlite3BtreeRollback's tripCode), then cleans up and clears the error (pager_unlock's part)

pager.go:*pager.rollbackToSavepoint.note: dbFileVers is restored as pager_playback_one_page restores it for page 1 (pager.c:2481-2484), approximated by a header or page-count change (drift-2026-11-12-5)

pager.go:*pager.savepoint.note: in the error state of a failed spill it returns pager.errCode, where sqlite3PagerOpenSavepoint does not test it (pager.c:6965-6974): a savepoint opened in a transaction that can only be rolled back has nothing to keep

pager.go:*pager.setCodec.note: replaces the codec chosen before the DB-file lock was held

pager.go:*pager.setLeafRule.note: records the file's leaf rule from its schema format

pager.go:*pager.truncateTo.note: backup destination shrink path (backup.c:530); discards writerCache pages beyond the new size

pager.go:*pager.tryCheckpoint.note: automatic checkpoint: PASSIVE only, as sqlite3WalDefaultHook's

pager.go:*pager.walBase.note: the open write transaction's starting position in the log, through wal.base

pager.go:*pager.walBaseFrame.note: frame number of the open write transaction's base, by wal.base's rule over atomics only: hasChanges, unwindWriter, commit's spill test, rollbackForClose

pager.go:SetCreateLegacyFormatForTest.note: test hook: create schema format 5 files

pager.go:keyProbePgno.note: the pages proveKeyAtOpen tries, spread over the database's pages; no SQLCipher counterpart (drift-2026-11-24-3)

pager.go:lockBtreePageCount.note: the page-count rule only (offset 28 vs the pager's count); a non-zero 24/92 mismatch is rejected, see drift-2026-11-11-2

pager.go:page1HeaderAtOpen.note: page 1 read again at open must name the file's magic family before its header is decoded; no SQLite counterpart (drift-2026-11-24-3)

pcache.go:*pcache.create.note: initial 'already cached?' probe via hashFind (pcache1FetchNoMutex); on allocate, hashInsert links into apHash (was pc.pages[pgno]=p). nPage replaces len(pages). Returns the xStress error without creating the page (sqlite3PcacheFetchStress).

pcache.go:*pcache.discard.note: lookup via hashFind; hashRemove (pcache1RemoveFromHash) clears page.inCache so a still-pinned discarded page is not re-LRU'd on release

pcache.go:*pcache.evictOne.note: pops LRU tail then hashRemove (was delete(pc.pages, p.pgno))

pcache.go:*pcache.fetch.note: lookup via hashFind (chained-bucket probe, pcache1FetchNoMutex step 1) then pin + lruRemove on a clean hit (pcache1PinPage)

pcache.go:*pcache.hashFind.note: chained-bucket probe apHash[pgno&(nHash-1)] walked by hashNext, the read-only half of pcache1FetchNoMutex step 1 (pcache1.c:1009-1010); shared by fetch/create. Closes NOTES §9 drift #2.

pcache.go:*pcache.hashInsert.note: links page at bucket head, sets page.inCache, bumps nPage, resizes at load factor 1.0 (pcache1.c:894 nPage>=nHash → pcache1ResizeHash)

pcache.go:*pcache.hashRemove.note: unlinks page from its bucket chain and clears page.inCache (pcache1.c:601-613); the inCache flag is a v2 addition for pages removed while pinned (no SQLite equivalent — SQLite forbids that)

pcache.go:*pcache.release.note: gates LRU insert on page.inCache (field read) instead of the former second map lookup (pc.pages[p.pgno]==p); overfull path calls hashRemove (pcache1RemoveFromHash). SQLite's pcache1Unpin adds to LRU unconditionally (its invariants forbid removing a pinned page); the inCache gate is the v2 ghost-page guard.

pcache.go:*pcache.resizeHash.note: doubles apHash and rehashes at load factor 1.0; power-of-two sizing (floor 256) so pgno&(nHash-1) is a mask (pcache1.c:535-567)

pcache.go:hashSizeFor.note: smallest power-of-two >= n and >= 256, matching pcache1ResizeHash's floor (pcache1.c:543)

pcache.go:newPcache.note: seeds apHash to a power-of-two size (>= maxPages, floor 256), mirroring pcache1Create which calls pcache1ResizeHash at creation (pcache1.c:789) to seed nHash=256

shm.go:newHeapShm.note: heap-backed shm constructor for single-process mode

shm_mmap.go:*mmapShm.regionsPerMap.note: the segments one mapping covers, for the size check of a lookup (shmFile)

shm_other.go:newPlatformShm.note: heap-backed shm fallback for platforms without mmap support

syncdir_other.go:*dirSync.set.note: no directory sync on Windows and js/wasm, as in SQLite's Windows VFS

syncdir_other.go:*dirSync.sync.note: the file's sync alone, as winSync syncs no directory

syncdir_unix.go:*dirSync.set.note: UNIXFILE_DIRSYNC, set on a journal or WAL descriptor opened with the create flag; the directory is that of the name the file was opened by (databaseDir), which a pager builds from the database's full name (FullPathname)

syncdir_unix.go:*dirSync.sync.note: fdatasync, then the directory at the first sync since set; racing first syncs wait for the directory sync

syncdir_unix.go:syncDir.note: the directory fsync unixSync does for a descriptor marked UNIXFILE_DIRSYNC; a directory that does not open, and the fsync's result, are ignored, as there

testseam.go:*DB.TestSeam.note: test seam for the packages above

testseam.go:TestSeam.Lock.note: test seam: a WAL lock through the handle's lock table

testseam.go:TestSeam.PeerPublish.note: test seam: another process's commit, as a begin sees it

testseam.go:TestSeam.TearHeader.note: test seam: the header as a writer between its two copies leaves it

wal.go:*beginBusy.retry.note: one begin's busy count, as sqlite3InvokeBusyHandler keeps nBusy (main.c:1770-1780): once the handler declines it is not asked again

wal.go:*wal.base.note: a position saved before the log was started over maps to frame 0 of the new log: the nCkpt test of wal.c:3829-3835 and the reloaded header of wal.c:3775

wal.go:*wal.beginReadHdrBusy.note: the begin's busy loop for SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY (btree.c:3730-3737), at the WAL read begin so open's page-1 read is covered too

wal.go:*wal.beginReadHdrRetry.note: one read begin attempt: walTryBeginRead's WAL_RETRY loop

wal.go:*wal.checkpointWithMode.note: includes the salt re-check after read lock 0 (version-3.52.0 wal.c:2256-2267); copies frames verbatim as walCheckpoint does (wal.c:2311-2315), except that page 1 reaches the main file with the keyed KDF salt (drift-2026-11-21-19)

wal.go:*wal.committedSize.note: the size a commit records: the pager's, or the last commit's for a caller that passes none

wal.go:*wal.doResetWAL.note: starts the log over; called by restartLogLocked and by a TRUNCATE checkpoint

wal.go:*wal.flushHeader.note: lazy WAL header flush on first write (any-store optimization)

wal.go:*wal.indexReadHdr.note: validated header read; rebuilds the wal-index under the write lock when the header is invalid, and returns the rebuild's error as walIndexReadHdr returns walIndexRecover's (wal.c:2724)

wal.go:*wal.initHeaderStateLocked.note: lazy WAL header init without disk write; returns the wal-index header's publication error

wal.go:*wal.pos.note: frame count, checksums and log generation (aWalData, wal.c:3811-3815)

wal.go:*wal.readFramePage.note: readFrame for a page number the caller resolved; decrypts with the database's integrity hook

wal.go:*wal.readFramePageHook.note: readFramePage with the integrity hook as an argument: the open's key proof passes its own (drift-2026-11-24-3)

wal.go:*wal.resetIReCksumIfPast.note: ports the iReCksum>mxFrame reset fragment of sqlite3WalSavepointUndo (wal.c:3849-3851)

wal.go:*wal.restartCandidate.note: the lock-free part of the restart test: no frame of this transaction in the log, nBackfill == mxFrame > 0

wal.go:*wal.restartHeaderStateLocked.note: header half of a WAL restart: mxFrame 0, hdr.nPage kept, salt1+1 and a random salt2; nCkpt stays 0 and aFrameCksum is the new WAL header's checksum (drift-98). Returns the publication's error, which walRestartHdr, writing the mapped header in place, cannot have

wal.go:*wal.restartLogLocked.note: writer-side log restart before a transaction's first frames (wal.c:3870-3888); explicit nBackfill==mxFrame test; also try-locks the checkpoint lock (drift-2026-11-12-2); keeps reader slot 0 (drift-2026-11-12-3)

wal.go:*wal.rewriteChecksums.note: in-tx frame-reuse checksum-chain rewrite (wal.c:3966-4009), called from writeFrames

wal.go:*wal.syncFile.note: every sync of the WAL file; the first since open syncs the directory too (UNIXFILE_DIRSYNC set by wal.open, as unixOpen sets it on every WAL opened with the create flag)

wal.go:*wal.waitReadersAndTruncate.note: RESTART/TRUNCATE tail (wal.c:2357-2382): RESTART only waits for reader slots 1-4, TRUNCATE also resets the header and truncates; a busy reader lock is the checkpoint's result

wal.go:*wal.writeFrames.note: appended frames staged and written in chunks of up to walFrameBatchMax, not two writes per frame (drift-2026-11-11-10)

wal.go:*wal.writeFramesMem.note: in-memory WAL fast path (no SQLite counterpart)

wal.go:*walIndex.getLatest.note: cache-invalidation lookup; no direct SQLite counterpart

wal.go:*walIndex.liveNBackfill.note: the shared pInfo->nBackfill that the reset and completeness tests read (wal.c:2355-2360), not the process-local mirror

wal.go:*walIndex.mapSegmentForLookup.note: a segment missing from the file fails the lookup; a writer's lookup does not extend the file either, where C's extend flag is pWal->writeLock (drift-92)

wal.go:*walIndex.prepareHeader.note: first half: fills wi.hdr and its checksum

wal.go:*walIndex.readHeaderState.note: walIndexTryHdr plus walIndexReadHdr's version gate: a consistent header of another wal-index version is refused, not torn (wal.c:2740-2741)

wal.go:*walIndex.rollbackToFrame.note: walCleanupHash analogue — discards pageMap entries above the target frame. The in-tx checksum-chain rewrite is a separate, ported function (wal.rewriteChecksums <- walRewriteChecksums)

wal.go:DefaultBusyTimeout.note: port of sqliteDefaultBusyCallback (main.c) — not in canonical sqlite_funcs list

wal.go:frameReadErr.note: the error of a failed frame read: ErrWALShortRead for a short read (SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ from unixRead), the read's own error otherwise (drift-2026-07-10-1)

wal.go:shmLookupFileSize.note: nReqRegion*szRegion: the file size a lookup needs before it maps a segment, the end of the segment's mapping group

wal.go:walPageChecksum.note: CRC32 helper (test-only); not used by WAL protocol

walchange.go:*wal.announce.note: an own header is known before it is published, as pWal->hdr is written first (wal.c:4243-4250, 2151-2154); a reset over an unseen header owes a step (wal.c:4399-4406); a recovery always does (wal.c:2724-2725)

walchange.go:*wal.changeEpoch.note: the epoch and whether a snapshot is exact for it

walchange.go:*wal.noteSnapshot.note: the *pChanged test of wal.c:2624-2626 and pager_reset's iDataVersion++ (pager.c:1773), against the process-wide change state (drift-2026-11-13-1)

walchange.go:*wal.publishHeader.note: walIndex.prepareHeader + storeHeader between announce and settle; sets iChange

walchange.go:*wal.settle.note: any-store: decides the change state from the live header on every way out of a publication (drift-2026-11-13-1)

walchange.go:*walChange.exact.note: any-store: a snapshot holds exactly the changes the epoch counts (drift-2026-11-13-1)

writer_gate.go:*writerGate.close.note: any-store: closes the gate and waits for the write transaction's call in flight; C takes the connection mutex, main.c sqlite3Close (drift-2026-11-21-25)

writer_gate.go:*writerGate.closed.note: any-store: whether Close has closed the gate (drift-2026-11-21-25)

writer_gate.go:*writerGate.enter.note: any-store: counts a call of the write transaction in by compare-and-swap, or refuses it uncounted once Close closed the gate and no call is in flight; C holds the connection mutex for the step, vdbeapi.c sqlite3_step (drift-2026-11-21-25)

writer_gate.go:*writerGate.leave.note: any-store: counts a call out and wakes a waiting Close (drift-2026-11-21-25)

writer_gate.go:CloseState.EndedByClose.note: any-store: whether DB.Close has closed the writer gate, so ended a write transaction still open (drift-2026-11-21-25)

writer_gate.go:newWriterGate.note: any-store: the pager's writer gate, open (drift-2026-11-21-25)
